title: Language-neutral concept ids — Cross-Language Concept Search
description: Concept search replaces words with language-neutral identifiers, so 'dog', 'perro', and 'chien' all become CONCEPT-042. Each concept carries a preferred term per language plus synonym lists, forming a small multilingual thesaurus. Queries and documents meet at the concept layer, never needing to share a language.

title: Dictionary-based query translation — Cross-Language Concept Search
description: The simplest cross-language method translates each query term through a bilingual dictionary and searches the translated terms. It handles one-to-many translations by OR-ing all senses, which raises recall at some precision cost. Dictionary coverage limits quality, so rare terms often fall back to transliteration.
provenance: Public methodology — standard computer-science technique documented in the technical literature; fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Pivot-language bridging — Cross-Language Concept Search
description: When no direct dictionary exists for a language pair, both sides translate through a pivot language, usually English. 'Haus' becomes 'house' becomes 'maison', chaining two dictionaries. Pivoting multiplies ambiguity at each hop, so it suits recall-oriented exploration more than precision tasks.
provenance: Public methodology — standard computer-science technique documented in the technical literature; fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Multilingual embeddings — Cross-Language Concept Search
description: Multilingual sentence embeddings place translations near each other in one shared vector space. A query embeds in its own language and retrieves nearest document vectors regardless of their language. No dictionaries are needed, but quality depends on the embedding model's training coverage.
provenance: Public methodology — standard computer-science technique documented in the technical literature; fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Cross-lingual explicit semantic analysis — Cross-Language Concept Search
description: CL-ESA represents texts as vectors over Wikipedia articles, using interlanguage links to align dimensions. A Spanish query and an English document share dimensions through articles existing in both languages. The method needs only Wikipedia, making it practical for many language pairs.
provenance: Public methodology — standard computer-science technique documented in the technical literature; fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Handling untranslatable terms — Cross-Language Concept Search
description: Culture-specific terms like 'saudade' have no single-word equivalent; systems keep the source term and add a gloss. Retrieval then matches the gloss terms in the target language plus any borrowed usages. Explicit gap-handling beats silent mistranslation for precision.
provenance: Public methodology — standard computer-science technique documented in the technical literature; fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Transliteration for proper names — Cross-Language Concept Search
description: Names cross scripts by sound, not dictionary: 'Moscow' and 'Moskva' need transliteration rules. Systems apply script-specific romanization tables before phonetic or fuzzy matching. Without transliteration, name search across scripts fails completely.
provenance: Public methodology — standard computer-science technique documented in the technical literature; fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Sense disambiguation across languages — Cross-Language Concept Search
description: 'Bank' translates differently as a river edge versus a financial institution; picking the wrong sense mistranslates the query. Disambiguation uses surrounding query terms to select the sense whose translations co-occur. Even a two-word query usually carries enough context to pick correctly.
provenance: Public methodology — standard computer-science technique documented in the technical literature; fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Comparable corpora mining — Cross-Language Concept Search
description: Comparable corpora (same-topic texts in two languages, not translations) yield translation pairs via context similarity. Words sharing similar co-occurrence patterns across languages are likely translations. This bootstraps dictionaries for language pairs with no parallel text.
provenance: Public methodology — standard computer-science technique documented in the technical literature; fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Ontology alignment — Cross-Language Concept Search
description: Domain ontologies in different languages align by matching structure plus label translations. Equivalent classes merge, giving one concept hierarchy queryable from any language. Aligned ontologies power cross-language faceted browsing in technical archives.

title: Mixed-language documents — Cross-Language Concept Search
description: Real archives mix languages within one document; language identification runs per paragraph or sentence. Each span is then indexed under its own language's terms plus shared concept ids. Span-level detection keeps code-switched documents retrievable from every language side.

title: Evaluation with multilingual topics — Cross-Language Concept Search
description: Cross-language retrieval is tested with topics written in one language and relevance judgments over multilingual pools. Metrics like MAP are computed per source language and averaged. Separate per-language scores reveal whether one language's pipeline lags the rest.

title: Script normalization — Cross-Language Concept Search
description: Before any matching, text is normalized to one Unicode form (usually NFC) so composed and decomposed characters compare equal. Case folding follows the same step, using language-aware rules where needed. Skipping normalization silently splits what users see as identical terms.

title: Low-resource language strategies — Cross-Language Concept Search
description: Languages with little training data borrow from relatives: shared subword vocabularies transfer across similar languages. Rule-based morphological analyzers, cheap to build, handle the agglutinative languages embeddings miss. Pragmatic pipelines mix transfer learning with hand-built rules.

title: Concept feedback loops — Cross-Language Concept Search
description: Relevance feedback in concept space adds the concepts of judged-relevant documents to the query. Because concepts are language-neutral, feedback from an English document improves Spanish retrieval. Cross-language feedback compounds faster than monolingual feedback.
